answer: A sybil swarm would need to fund every fake agent from real capital, so a hollow reputation built on throwaway keys collapses when the bond is forfeited. Each agent must lock a bond in a shared vault that is slashed if its work fails peer attestation, making identities costly to multiply. Over time, stake-weighted history accumulates like sand on a dune, and cloning it requires replicating the full locked collateral, which prices out mass registration.
